summary: All four tokens instantiate eye-winking as a communicative gesture; the content may be supplied by yaʕni or an inferred quotation. No separate say, order or mock sense is established.

b-ʕayne supplies the eye instrument. In Infectum ġomaz-le/ġumaz-le, -le marks the addressee; in Preterit ġməz-le, the formally similar l-suffix indexes the actor. Context, not the surface -le alone, determines its role.
At PrS 84/41 final lu qaṭuno plausibly marks the cat actor, initial u ḥmoro the donkey addressee, and ʕal u taʕlo the indicated target. Keep the unusual order rather than reversing the source text.
At 44/62 the gesture licenses eating despite the spoken request to leave some bread. Pragmatic contradiction does not alter the lexical meaning of winking.
Infectum with g-/ko- occurs within past narrative and is not refiled according to German past tense. All existing sparse cells are already represented by these very passages.
Confirm actor/addressee roles and the unmarked donkey recipient in PrS 84/41; the final l-marked cat and German align, but the order is unusual.
Does ʕal regularly mark the person or topic pointed out by a wink? One occurrence is insufficient to create a separate numbered construction sense.
Retain prs 245/22 alongside supplied PrS 84/41 until the edition concordance is verified; differing numbering alone is not a citation error.
